WHAT SCRIPTURE SAYS
What Scripture says of him
“Ben-hadad king of Syria gathered all his host, and went up, and besieged Samaria.” 2 Kings 6:24
The siege brought a famine in which “an ass’s head was sold for fourscore pieces of silver”. 2 Kings 6:25
“The Lord had made the host of the Syrians to hear a noise of chariots, and a noise of horses”, and they fled, leaving their camp. 2 Kings 7:6–7
Sick at Damascus, he sent Hazael to Elisha: “Shall I recover of this disease?” 2 Kings 8:7–8
Hazael called him “Thy son Ben-hadad king of Syria” before the prophet. 2 Kings 8:9
“On the morrow, that he took a thick cloth, and dipped it in water, and spread it on his face, so that he died: and Hazael reigned in his stead.” 2 Kings 8:15
DEALINGS
Dealings with God's people
He asked through Hazael for a word from Israel's God: “enquire of the LORD by him, saying, Shall I recover of this disease?” 2 Kings 8:8
Samaria's famine under his siege: the king of Israel “had sackcloth within upon his flesh”. 2 Kings 6:30
Plenty after his flight: “a measure of fine flour was sold for a shekel, and two measures of barley for a shekel, according to the word of the LORD”. 2 Kings 7:16

OUTSIDE THE BIBLE
DATES DIFFER
When was it?
PLACED BY THE ASSYRIAN RECORDS AND SCRIPTURE
No years given[1][2]

No year of his own is known. The siege story names no king of Israel; the chapters around it are set in the reign of Joram son of Ahab (852–841 BC on Thiele, McFall and Young). Hazael, who took his throne, was already king of Damascus when Shalmaneser III fought him in his eighteenth year (841 BC).
Ben-hadad himself, by accident
Luther, Schultz, Geddes and Boothroyd, as reported by the Pulpit Commentary
These commentators supposed Ben-hadad laid the wet cloth on his own face to cool himself and was suffocated; the Pulpit Commentary calls this “very unlikely”.[28]
A servant
H. Ewald, History of Israel, as reported by the Pulpit Commentary and Ellicott
Ewald introduced a bath-servant as the one who killed the king; both commentaries reject it, noting that Hazael is named at the end of the verse as the new king.[28][29]
IN SCRIPTURE
Every passage
CHAPTERS · 3
2 Kings 6 2 Kings 7 2 Kings 8
PASSAGES · 2
WHAT SCRIPTURE DOES NOT SAY
Scripture never gives this Ben-hadad's father, his age, or the length of his reign.
2 Kings 5–6 speaks of “the king of Syria” without naming him; that he is this Ben-hadad is a reading, not a statement.
Scripture does not name the king of Israel during the siege of Samaria.
The Assyrian records used here never name a Ben-hadad; they name Hadad-ezer (or Bir-idri) and then Hazael.
IDENTIFICATIONS THIS PAGE RELIES ON

From the textThis page follows the site's record for the Ben-hadad named in 2 Kings 6:24 and 8:7–9. The unnamed “king of Syria” of 2 Kings 5:1–6:23 (Naaman's master, the hunt for Elisha at Dothan) is left off this page: the text does not name him, and the site's record does not include him. 2 Kings 6:24 2 Kings 8:7–9 2 Kings 5:1 2 Kings 6:8

From the textWhether he is the Ben-hadad of 1 Kings 20 is a question with views below; whether that king is the Hadad-ezer of Shalmaneser III's records is set out on the page of Asa's Ben-hadad. 1 Kings 20:1
